tldr: Mastercard Agent Pay is a proprietary card-network program. Registered agents get scoped agentic tokens, sign their web requests, and can carry Verifiable Intent proof of what the user approved. Named transactions are pilots.
whyItExists: A card network cannot tell an agent purchase from a human one, or from fraud, when the agent types a stolen-looking card number into a form. Agent Pay gives the network a way to know which agent is buying, under whose authority and within which limits: agents register and are certified, they receive tokens instead of card numbers, the tokens carry the consumer's limits, and merchants can check a signature on the agent's web request. Verifiable Intent adds a signed record of what the user approved, so issuers and merchants have evidence when a purchase is questioned.

whatItIsNot.text: Not AP2. AP2 is an open mandate protocol that Google launched and contributed to the FIDO Alliance; Agent Pay is Mastercard's card-network program. They meet only through Verifiable Intent, which reuses AP2's mandate type strings.
Not the same thing as a Visa agentic token. Both networks use the words, but Mastercard Agentic Tokens and Visa's agentic network tokens are separate products from separate networks.
Not an open protocol. Mastercard sets the rules alone, and the Acceptance Framework specification it refers developers to is not public. Only Verifiable Intent is open.
Not at scale yet. The transactions Mastercard names are pilots, controlled trials or first transactions, and it publishes no volume or value figures.

Not a new token platform. Agentic tokens build on Mastercard tokenization, and Mastercard's Agent Pay developer page, as read on 2026-10-21, lists network tokenization through MDES among Agent Pay's technologies.

Not a new liability regime. Mastercard says standard chargeback rights apply. Its public rules (2026-06-02 edition) point participants to Mastercard Agent Pay Program Standards that are not public; no agent-specific reason code, liability shift or interchange category is published (as of 2026-10-21).
Not a payments SDK. The Mastercard Developers Agent Toolkit is an MCP server that reads documentation and API specifications and makes no payment calls.

changedRecently.text: Santander and Mastercard completed Europe's first live end-to-end agent payment, in a controlled environment and explicitly not a commercial rollout.
Stripe extended Shared Payment Tokens to carry Mastercard agentic network tokens.
Mastercard announced Verifiable Intent and opened the agent-intent/verifiable-intent repository.
Verifiable Intent pull request 23 renamed constraint keys to the mandate.payment.* form without a new version number.
Mastercard contributed Verifiable Intent to the FIDO Alliance on the day Google contributed AP2.
Mastercard said all its European issuers are enabled for Agent Pay at network level, with 36 named banks completing controlled live transactions.
Mastercard announced Agent Pay for Machines for high-frequency, low-value machine payments across cards, accounts and stablecoins.

Mastercard named the Agent Pay Trust Framework and published its white paper, said a probability score for agent-initiated transactions is rolling out for US testing, and named Skyfire as a Know Your Agent partner.
Mastercard opened Agent Pay for Machines Early Access with buyer- and seller-side APIs, a toolkit and a sandbox, and said AP4M builds on x402.
